heroSummary: The Bambu Lab A1 handles Prusament PETG exceptionally well right out of the box using its stock stainless steel nozzle and open-frame architecture. With an effective volumetric flow limit of 15 mm³/s, the printer reliably sustains speeds up to 179 mm/s at standard 0.2mm layer heights.
bedSurfaceRecommendation: Textured PEI Plate with no adhesive needed, or Smooth PEI Plate with glue stick as a release agent
slicerTweaks: Set Max Volumetric Speed to 15 mm³/s in the filament settings to prevent under-extrusion at high print speeds.
Enable 'Wipe while retracting' (2 mm distance) and activate 'Avoid crossing walls' to minimize fine PETG stringing.
Set the nozzle temperature to 250°C for the first layer and 248°C for subsequent layers to ensure optimal layer fusion on the stainless steel hotend.
Limit cooling fan speed between 20% and 50% with layer times below 30 seconds to maintain maximum inter-layer bonding strength.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Stringing and fine whisker buildup during travel moves
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: PETG absorbs ambient moisture quickly, decreasing viscosity, combined with aggressive non-print travel moves without wipe.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Dry filament at 65°C for 6 hours; set retraction distance to 0.8 mm at 35 mm/s and enable 'Wipe on Loops' in OrcaSlicer.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: First layer tearing or parts bonding too strongly to Smooth PEI
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: PETG has high molecular adhesion to smooth PEI coatings, risking plate damage, or nozzle Z-offset dragging through molten bead.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Switch to the Bambu Textured PEI plate, or apply a thin layer of PVP glue stick on smooth PEI as a sacrificial release barrier.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Matte finish and weak layer-to-layer strength at high speeds
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Volumetric flow bottleneck causing melt zone starvation and excessive part cooling fan speed exceeding 60%.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Cap volumetric speed to 15 mm³/s, lower Max Fan Speed to 50%, and raise printing temperature to 252°C.

faq.question: Does the Bambu Lab A1 need an enclosure to print Prusament PETG reliably?
faq.answer: No, Prusament PETG does not require an enclosure and prints best on an open-frame printer like the A1 to prevent heat creep and excessive chamber heat.

faq.question: Can the stock stainless steel nozzle on the A1 withstand Prusament PETG?
faq.answer: Yes, standard Prusament PETG is non-abrasive, so the stock stainless steel nozzle will handle it without accelerated wear.

faq.question: Why is the maximum printing speed capped at 179 mm/s?
faq.answer: The flow is capped to respect Prusament PETG's safe volumetric limit of 15 mm³/s on the A1 hotend at standard 0.42mm line width and 0.2mm layer height.

faq.question: Do I need glue stick on the Bambu Textured PEI plate for Prusament PETG?
faq.answer: No, textured PEI releases PETG cleanly once cooled below 35°C; glue is only recommended on smooth PEI sheets as a release agent to prevent surface tear-out.
